newsitem.title: USA: Tank fire extinguished at Houston-area plant.
newsitem.headline: Tank fire extinguished at Houston-area plant.

text.p: A tank fire at Petro-United Chemical Co's Bayport, Texas plant was extinguished on Thursday and there were no injuries in the blast, officials said
At least one neighboring plant was evacuated and firefighters from several nearby petro-chemical facilities were called in to battle the blaze, officials said.
"There are no injuries, all notifications have been made and the fire is out," a Petro-United plant spokesman said.
The explosion, which rattled windows in nearby houses and was heard by workers on a tugboat operating nearby, occured while chemicals were being transferred in the tank, the spokesman said.
Additional details were not immediately available.
"All we know is (there is) a tank fire," a fire department dispatcher said.

"We had a tank fire at 7:10 a.m. central time (1310 GMT) in a small (storage) tank, about 12,500 barrels (capacity). It wasn't at capacity, though, it was slightly over half full at the time (with) propylene oxide," a feedstock for making plastics, said a Petro-United Chemical Co representative.
"We had the fire out by 8:20 a.m. We have no idea what caused it yet, we are still in assess mode at the moment. The main thing was there were no injuries," he added.

The plant, which has capacity to store slightly more than two million barrels of product, is shut down until the cause of the fire can be determined, the official said. There is no processing operations at the Bayport site, only terminal storage.
